title: Characterization of the response of taurine protons to PRESS at 9.4 T for Resolving choline and Determining taurine T2

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Point‐resolved spectroscopy (PRESS), characterized by two TEs (TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub> and TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>), can be employed to perform animal magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) studies at 9.4 T. Taurine (Tau) and choline (Cho) are relevant metabolites that can be measured by MRS. In this work, the response of the <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>‐coupled protons of Tau as a function of PRESS TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub> and TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> was characterized at 9.4 T to achieve two objectives. The first was to determine two TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub> and TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> combinations that could be used to obtain <jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub>‐corrected measures of Tau (3.42 ppm) that were minimally influenced by <jats:italic>J</jats:italic> coupling. The second was to exploit the Tau <jats:italic>J</jats:italic> coupling to find a timing combination that minimized the 3.25‐ppm Tau signal to enable the Cho (3.22 ppm) resonance to be resolved from the overlapping Tau signal. The response of Tau protons was investigated both numerically and experimentally. It was numerically determined that the timings {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {17 ms, 10 ms} and {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {80 ms, 70 ms} yielded similar 3.42‐ppm Tau resonance areas (5% difference), rendering them suitable for Tau <jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub> determination. {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {25 ms, 50 ms} was found to yield minimal 3.25‐ppm Tau signal, reducing its interference with Cho. The efficacy of the timings was demonstrated on phantom solutions and <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic> in four Sprague Dawley rats. LCModel was employed to analyse the <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic> spectra and Tau <jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub> values were estimated by fitting the Tau peak areas obtained with {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {17 ms, 10 ms} and {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {80 ms, 70 ms} to a monoexponentially decaying function. An average Tau <jats:italic>T</jats:italic><jats:sub>2</jats:sub> of 106 ms (standard deviation, 12 ms) was obtained. LCModel analysis of rat spectra obtained with {TE<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>, TE<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>} = {25 ms, 50 ms} demonstrated negligible levels of Tau signal, compared with that obtained with short TE.</jats:p>
